why: Aaron was Moses' brother; both were sons of Amram and Jochebed.
The LORD sent Aaron to speak for Moses, and together they stood before Pharaoh and brought Israel out of Egypt.
Pharaoh refused the LORD's word that Moses and Aaron brought him, drove them from his presence, and chased Israel with his army.
Miriam was Aaron's sister, a daughter of Amram and Jochebed.
Eleazar was Aaron's son, and Aaron's priestly garments were put on him when Aaron died.
Korah and his company rose against Aaron seeking the priesthood, and the LORD chose Aaron when both offered incense before Him.
Abel was Cain's younger brother, both born to Eve.
Cain rose up against his brother Abel in the field and killed him, because his own works were evil and his brother's righteous.
Adam and Eve had Cain and then his brother Abel; after Abel was killed, Seth was born to Adam in his place.
Eve bore Abel after Cain, and later named Seth as another seed in place of Abel.
After Abimelech restored Sarah, Abraham prayed to God and God healed Abimelech, his wife and his maidservants.
Abimelech asked Abraham to swear not to deal falsely with him, and the two made a covenant at Beersheba.
Abimelech came to Isaac and asked for an oath between them, and they swore one to another and parted in peace.
Sarah was Abraham's wife; she went with him to Canaan and bore him Isaac in his old age.
Isaac was Abraham's son, born to him in his old age; Abraham bound him on the altar at God's command and later gave him all he had.
Lot was the son of Abraham's brother Haran, and went with Abraham into Canaan.
Abraham armed his servants and brought Lot back when he was taken captive, and God remembered Abraham and sent Lot out of Sodom.
Sarah gave her maid Hagar to Abraham to be his wife, and Hagar bore him Ishmael.
Ishmael was Abraham's son, borne to him by Hagar.
Melchisedec, priest of the most high God, blessed Abraham, and Abraham gave him tithes of all.
God made the woman from Adam and brought her to him; Adam called his wife Eve, and she bore him children.
Adam knew Eve his wife, and she bore Cain.
Balak sent for Balaam and consulted him, and Balaam answered him and taught Balak to cast a stumblingblock before Israel.
Joseph and Benjamin were the two sons of Rachel, and Joseph wept over his brother when he saw him in Egypt.
Benjamin was Jacob's youngest son, born to Rachel.
Jacob loved Benjamin, the child of his old age, and held him back from Egypt, for his life was bound up in the lad's life.
Rachel bore Benjamin and died in childbirth, naming him Benoni; his father called him Benjamin.
Eve bore Cain and said, I have gotten a man from the LORD.
Joshua and Caleb together tore their clothes and urged the people to go up into the land, and of the spies only they lived, because they wholly followed the LORD.
Rachel gave Bilhah to Jacob so that she might have children by her, and when Dan was born Rachel said God had given her a son and named him.
Bilhah bore Jacob a son, Dan.
Pharaoh's daughter drew Moses out of the water with compassion, and he became her son and was named by her.
She was the daughter of Pharaoh, the king who ordered every Hebrew son cast into the river.
Simeon and Levi were Dinah's brothers, and they took their swords and slew the men of Shechem because their sister was defiled.
Dinah was Jacob's daughter, born to Leah.
Leah bore Dinah to Jacob.
Moses and Eleazar the priest together numbered Israel, heard the people's cases, and divided the spoil as the LORD commanded.
Eleazar married one of the daughters of Putiel, and she bore him Phinehas.
Enoch begat Methuselah and walked with God after his birth.
Ephraim was Joseph's second son, born in Egypt and named by Joseph.
Jacob told Joseph that Ephraim and Manasseh, born in Egypt, were his own, as Reuben and Simeon.
Jacob laid his right hand on Ephraim, blessed him in the name of God, and set him before Manasseh.
Manasseh and Ephraim were the two sons born to Joseph in Egypt.
Esau and Jacob were twin sons of Isaac and Rebekah.
Jacob took Esau's birthright and then his blessing, and Esau hated him for it.
Esau was Isaac's firstborn, one of the twins Rebekah bore him.
Isaac loved Esau, because he did eat of his venison.
Rebekah bore Esau and Jacob as twins.
Leah gave her maid Zilpah to Jacob as wife, and when Zilpah bore Gad, Leah named him.
Zilpah, Leah's maid, bore Jacob a son, Gad.
Reuben and Gad were both among the twelve sons of Jacob.
Hagar was Sarah's Egyptian handmaid, and Sarah was her mistress.
When Hagar conceived she despised her mistress, Sarah dealt hardly with her, and Sarah later had Hagar and her son cast out so he would not be heir with Isaac.
Hagar bore Ishmael to Abraham, and wandered with him in the wilderness when they were sent away.
Ham was one of the three sons of Noah who went forth from the ark.
Shem and Ham were sons of Noah.
Ham and Japheth were sons of Noah.
Isaac took Rebekah, and she became his wife, and he loved her.
Jacob was one of the twin sons Rebekah bore Isaac.
Isaac blessed Jacob, who came disguised as Esau, and later blessed him again with the blessing of Abraham.
Sarah bore Isaac to Abraham in his old age, at the set time God had spoken.
Isaac and Ishmael were both sons of Abraham, and buried him together.
When Sarah saw Ishmael mocking, she had him cast out, saying he would not be heir with her son Isaac.
Laban was the brother of Jacob's mother Rebekah, and gave Jacob his daughters Leah and Rachel as wives.
Jacob served Laban fourteen years for his daughters and six years for his cattle.
Jacob served seven years for Rachel because he loved her, and Laban gave her to him to wife.
Laban gave Leah to Jacob in place of Rachel, and she became his wife and bore him sons.
Joseph was the son Rachel bore Jacob.
Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, mourned him as dead, and fell on his neck when he saw him alive.
Rebekah bore Jacob and Esau as twins.
Rebekah loved Jacob, had him take Esau's blessing, and sent him away when Esau planned to kill him.
Jacob blessed Pharaoh when Joseph set him before him, and blessed him again as he left.
Judah was the fourth son Leah bore Jacob.
Japheth was one of the three sons of Noah who went forth from the ark.
Shem and Japheth were sons of Noah.
Jethro was Moses' father-in-law, who gave him his daughter Zipporah.
Jethro saw Moses judging the people alone and gave him counsel to appoint rulers, and Moses hearkened to his voice.
Aaron and the elders of Israel came to eat bread with Moses' father-in-law Jethro before God.
Pharaoh set Joseph over his house and all the land of Egypt, second only to the throne.
Joseph and Judah were both among the twelve sons of Jacob.
Judah urged his brothers to sell their brother Joseph to the Ishmeelites, and Joseph later named himself to them as the brother whom they sold into Egypt.
Joseph and Reuben were both among the twelve sons of Jacob.
Reuben delivered Joseph out of his brothers' hands, so that they did not kill him, to restore him to his father.
Joseph named his firstborn Manasseh, for God had made him forget all his toil.
Potiphar bought Joseph and made him overseer over his house and all he had.
God remembered Rachel, and she bore a son and called him Joseph.
Joshua was Moses' minister, who went up the mount with him and served him from his youth.
At the LORD's command Moses laid his hands on Joshua and gave him a charge before the congregation, and Joshua was full of the spirit of wisdom.
Judah and Benjamin were both among the twelve sons of Jacob.
Judah became surety for Benjamin to his father, and offered to remain a bondman in Egypt in Benjamin's place.
Judah took Tamar as wife for his firstborn Er, and she later bore Judah twin sons, Pharez and Zarah.
Leah bore Judah and said, Now will I praise the LORD.
Korah gathered men against Moses and Aaron, saying they lifted themselves above the congregation, and Moses told him he was seeking the priesthood also.
Leah was Laban's elder daughter, and he gave her to Jacob as wife.
Rachel was Laban's younger daughter.
Rebekah had a brother, Laban, who with their father agreed she should be Isaac's wife.
Leah and Rachel were Laban's two daughters.
Rachel envied her sister's children, and Leah said Rachel had taken her husband; they strove for Jacob's love.
Leah bore Reuben, her firstborn, and said, Surely the LORD hath looked upon my affliction.
Jacob told Joseph that Ephraim and Manasseh, born in Egypt, were his own, as Reuben and Simeon.
Jacob blessed Manasseh with Ephraim in the name of God, laying his left hand on Manasseh's head.
Miriam was the sister of Aaron and Moses, a daughter of Amram and Jochebed.
Pharaoh refused the LORD's word that Moses brought, threatened to kill Moses if he saw his face again, and chased Israel with his army.
When Pharaoh heard Moses had killed an Egyptian, he sought to slay Moses, and Moses fled from his face to Midian.
Shem was one of the three sons of Noah who went forth from the ark.
Potiphar was an officer of Pharaoh, captain of the guard.
Phinehas was the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest.
Reuben was Jacob's firstborn, born to Leah.
Sihon refused Moses' request to pass through and came out against Israel to fight, and Israel smote him and took his land.
Simeon was the second son Leah bore Jacob.
Joseph and Simeon were both among the twelve sons of Jacob.
Leah bore Simeon and said, The LORD hath heard that I was hated.
Adam begat Seth in his own likeness, after his image.
Eve bore Seth and said God had appointed her another seed instead of Abel.
Eve bore Seth as another seed God gave her in place of her son Abel, whom Cain slew.
Jethro gave Moses his daughter Zipporah, and she bore him sons.
Zipporah was the daughter of Jethro, priest of Midian.
Simeon and Levi were Leah's second and third sons, and Jacob called them brethren in his words over them.
Leah bore Levi and said, Now this time will my husband be joined unto me.
Levi was the third son Leah bore Jacob.
Simeon and Levi were Dinah's brothers, and they took their swords and slew the men of Shechem because their sister was defiled.
Leah bore Jacob a fifth son and called him Issachar.
Reuben and Issachar were both sons of Leah, among the twelve sons of Jacob.
Leah bore Jacob a sixth son and called him Zebulun.
Issachar and Zebulun were Leah's fifth and sixth sons.
Bilhah, Rachel's maid, bore Naphtali, and Rachel named him, saying she had wrestled with her sister and prevailed.
Dan and Naphtali were the sons of Bilhah, Rachel's handmaid.
Zilpah, Leah's maid, bore Jacob a second son, and Leah named him Asher.
Gad and Asher were the sons of Zilpah, Leah's handmaid.
Abiathar fled to David and stayed with him, bringing the ephod to inquire of the LORD for him, and served as priest under King David.
Saul had Abiathar's father and the priests of Nob slain, and Abiathar escaped to David, who told him that the one who sought David's life sought his as well.
Zadok and Abiathar were the priests together under David, carrying the ark of God and sending David word from Jerusalem during Absalom's revolt.
Abigail was the wife of Nabal of Maon.
After Nabal died, David sent for Abigail and she became his wife.
Gideon's concubine in Shechem bore him a son, and Gideon named him Abimelech.
Jotham was the youngest son of Jerubbaal, and he fled for fear of Abimelech his brother.
Abimelech slew his brothers and Jotham alone escaped, then cursed Abimelech and the men of Shechem, and God rendered Abimelech's wickedness.
Joab and Abishai were brothers, sons of Zeruiah.
Joab and Abishai led David's army together, slaying Abner and dividing the host between them against Ammon and Syria.
Abishai went down with David into Saul's camp, commanded a third of David's army, and saved David from the giant's son who sought to kill him.
Zeruiah, Abishai's mother, was a sister of David and his brothers.
Abishai pursued Abner after the battle at Gibeon, and Joab and Abishai slew Abner because he had slain their brother Asahel.
Abishai twice asked to kill Shimei for cursing David, and David forbade him both times.
David sent Abishai with the mighty men to pursue Sheba the son of Bichri, and they chased him to Abel.
Abner was the captain of Saul's host, sat by Saul's side, and lay by him in camp to keep him.
Abner was the son of Ner, Saul's uncle.
Abner, captain of Saul's host, took Ish-bosheth and made him king over all Israel, and made himself strong for the house of Saul.
After Ish-bosheth rebuked him over Rizpah, Abner swore to translate the kingdom from the house of Saul to David and went to bring all Israel over to him.
Abner and Joab led the two sides at Gibeon, and Joab later took Abner aside at Hebron and killed him for the blood of Asahel his brother.
Abner led the house of Saul against the servants of David at Gibeon and made himself strong for the house of Saul in the long war between the two houses.
Absalom was David's third son, born in Hebron to Maacah.
Absalom made himself king in Hebron and drove David from Jerusalem, and David said, my son seeketh my life.
Amnon and Absalom were sons of David born in Hebron, and scripture calls Amnon Absalom’s brother.
Absalom hated Amnon for forcing his sister Tamar, and two years later commanded his servants to kill him.
Tamar was Absalom's sister, and after Amnon forced her she remained desolate in her brother Absalom's house.
Joab sent the wise woman of Tekoah to the king and then went to Geshur and brought Absalom back to Jerusalem.
When Absalom rebelled, Joab took three darts and thrust them through Absalom's heart as he hung in the oak.
Absalom sent for Ahithophel, who counselled him to go in to his father's concubines and to pursue David at once, and his counsel was as the oracle of God to Absalom.
Hushai pledged himself to Absalom, then gave him counsel that defeated Ahithophel's and secretly sent word to David.
Joshua had Achan confess that he took the accursed thing, asked him why he had troubled Israel, and had him stoned in the valley of Achor.
David dwelt with Achish, who gave him Ziklag and made him keeper of his head, and Achish said David would be his servant for ever.
Ahithophel was the king's counsellor, and his counsel was esteemed both by David and by Absalom as if a man inquired at the oracle of God.
Ahithophel, David's counsellor, joined Absalom's conspiracy and counselled him to pursue David and smite the king only.
Hushai set his counsel against Ahithophel's before Absalom, and Absalom and Israel said the counsel of Hushai was better than the counsel of Ahithophel.
Amnon and Tamar were both children of David, and Tamar called him my brother.
Tamar came to Amnon's house at the king's word to make him food, and Amnon forced her, then hated her and had her put out.
Amnon was David's firstborn son, born in Hebron to Ahinoam.
Deborah called Barak to lead Israel against Sisera, went up with him to Kedesh, sent him down from Tabor, and sang with him after the victory.
Barak went down from mount Tabor against Sisera, discomfited his host, and pursued after him.
Bathsheba was the wife of Uriah the Hittite, and she mourned for her husband when he died.
After Uriah's death David sent for Bathsheba and she became his wife, and she bore him Solomon.
Benaiah was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites, David set him over his guard, and at David's command he brought Solomon to Gihon to be anointed king.
Boaz redeemed the inheritance and took Ruth the Moabitess to be his wife, and she bore him a son.
Naomi had a kinsman of her husband's, Boaz, of the family of Elimelech, and she called him one of our next kinsmen.
Boaz sent six measures of barley to Naomi so Ruth would not come to her empty, and bought all that was Elimelech's from Naomi's hand.
Moses sent Caleb from the wilderness of Paran to spy out the land, and Caleb stilled the people before Moses; Caleb later recalled that Moses the servant of the LORD sent him and swore him the land.
David stood before Saul as his armourbearer and played the harp for him, and Saul set him over the men of war.
Saul gave David his daughter Michal to wife, making David his son in law.
Saul became David's enemy continually, spoke of killing him, and sought him every day.
Jonathan loved David as his own soul and made a covenant with him, and David said Jonathan's love to him was wonderful.
Goliath cursed David by his gods and came against him, and David smote him with a stone and cut off his head.
Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed David in the midst of his brethren, and the Spirit of the LORD came upon David.
Nathan answered David about building the LORD's house and brought him God's word, rebuked him over Bathsheba, and came to him about Adonijah so that he made Solomon king.
Joab went up first against Jebus and was made chief and captain, and he was over the host of David.
Joab was a son of Zeruiah, a sister of David.
Saul gave Michal his daughter to David to wife, and David later demanded her back as my wife Michal.
Uriah the Hittite was among David's mighty men, and he would not go down to his house while the ark and Joab and the servants of his lord camped in the field.
David wrote to Joab by Uriah's own hand to set him in the forefront of the hottest battle, and Nathan said, thou hast killed Uriah the Hittite with the sword.
David was the youngest son of Jesse the Bethlehemite, who kept his father's sheep.
David showed kindness to Mephibosheth for Jonathan's sake, restored him all the land of Saul, and had him eat continually at the king's table, and later spared him.
Hushai was the king's companion, and at David's word he returned to Absalom as David's servant to defeat Ahithophel's counsel and sent David word to flee.
Shimei came out cursing David and cast stones at him, calling him a bloody man, and David later charged Solomon to bring his hoar head down to the grave with blood.
Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David with cedar trees, carpenters and masons, and they built David a house.
Scripture says Hiram king of Tyre was ever a lover of David.
Zadok was priest under David, carried the ark back to Jerusalem at the king's word during Absalom's revolt, and at David's command anointed Solomon.
Nabal railed on David's messengers and David swore to leave none of his males alive, and when the LORD smote Nabal, David blessed the LORD who had pleaded his cause.
Sheba led the men of Israel away from David, and David sent his servants to pursue him lest he do more harm than Absalom.
Deborah sent Barak against Sisera with the LORD's word that he would be delivered into his hand, saying the LORD would sell Sisera into the hand of a woman.
Samson loved a woman in the valley of Sorek whose name was Delilah.
Delilah took the Philistines' silver, pressed Samson until he told her his heart, and had his head shaved so the Philistines took him.
The LORD named Eleazar the priest and Joshua to divide the land, and they distributed the inheritances by lot together.
The child Samuel ministered unto the LORD before Eli the priest, ran to Eli when he was called, and Eli taught him to answer the LORD.
Eli told Hannah the God of Israel would grant her petition, and later blessed Elkanah and her, and the LORD gave her Samuel and then five more children.
The prophet Gad, David's seer, told David to depart into Judah, brought him the LORD's word after the census, and told him to build an altar on Araunah's threshing floor.
Jotham was the youngest son of Jerubbaal, and he spoke of how my father fought for you.
Goliath defied the armies of Israel, calling them servants to Saul, and Saul and all Israel were dismayed and greatly afraid.
Hannah bore a son and called him Samuel, lent him to the LORD at Shiloh, and made him a little coat every year.
David told Hushai to report all he heard to Zadok and Abiathar the priests, and Hushai told them Ahithophel's counsel so that it was sent to David.
David told Hushai to report all he heard to Zadok and Abiathar the priests, and Hushai told them Ahithophel's counsel so that it was sent to David.
Ish-bosheth reigned over Israel while David reigned over Judah, and there was long war between the house of Saul and the house of David.
Michal was Saul's daughter and Ish-bosheth was Saul's son, and Ish-bosheth sent and took her from Phaltiel when David demanded her.
Ish-bosheth was the son of Saul, made king over Israel after his father died.
Samuel came to Jesse in Bethlehem, sanctified him and his sons, and had Jesse's sons pass before him until David was brought and anointed.
Uriah served in Joab's army and spoke of my lord Joab, and at David's order Joab assigned him to a place where he knew valiant men were, and Uriah died.
Joab pursued Sheba and besieged him in Abel, and the city cut off Sheba's head and cast it out to Joab.
Jonathan was Saul's son; he stood up for David to his father, and Saul cast a javelin at him, and in their death they were not divided.
Jonathan, Saul's son, had a son that was lame of his feet, named Mephibosheth.
Joshua saved Rahab and her father's household alive when Jericho fell, because she hid the messengers he sent to spy out the city.
Manoah's wife bore a son and called him Samson, and Samson was buried in the burying place of Manoah his father.
Michal was Saul's daughter; Saul gave her to David to be a snare to him, and later gave her to Phalti.
Ruth the Moabitess was Naomi's daughter in law, the wife of her son.
Ruth clave unto Naomi and vowed, whither thou goest I will go, and the women said Ruth loved Naomi and was better to her than seven sons.
Samuel poured a vial of oil on Saul's head and anointed him captain over the LORD's inheritance.
Samuel rebuked Saul for offering the burnt offering and for sparing Amalek, and told him the LORD had rejected him from being king.
Tamar was the sister of David's sons, the king's daughter, and David sent her to Amnon's house.
Eglon oppressed Israel, and Ehud brought him a present, then thrust a dagger into his belly and killed him.
Micah consecrated the young Levite, who became his priest and dwelt in his house for wages, food and clothing.
When the Danites came, the priest's heart was glad and he took Micah's ephod, teraphim and graven image and went with them, and Micah cried, ye have taken away my gods which I made, and the priest.
Gilead begat Jephthah, the son of an harlot.
Jael took Sisera into her tent and, while he slept, smote the nail into his temples and killed him.
Jael went out to meet Barak as he pursued Sisera and showed him the man he sought, lying dead in her tent.
In the song Deborah sang to the LORD, she blessed Jael above women for killing Sisera.
Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, took Kirjath-sepher, and Caleb gave him Achsah his daughter to wife.
Abiathar the priest followed Adonijah and helped him in his bid to be king, and was at his feast when they cried, God save king Adonijah.
Solomon told Abiathar he was worthy of death for siding with Adonijah, but spared him and thrust him out from being priest.
Abijah was Rehoboam's son, and Rehoboam made him chief among his brethren to make him king after him.
There was war between Abijah and Jeroboam, and God smote Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah, so that Jeroboam never recovered strength in Abijah's days.
Asa was Abijah's son and reigned in his stead.
Solomon called Adonijah "mine elder brother."

Adonijah tried to make himself king, but the kingdom went to his brother Solomon, as Adonijah himself said; when he then asked for Abishag, Solomon saw it as asking for the kingdom and had him put to death.
When Solomon ordered Adonijah's death, Benaiah fell upon him and killed him.
Joab followed Adonijah and helped him in his bid to be king; scripture says Joab had turned after Adonijah.
Elijah confronted Ahab for forsaking the commandments of the LORD and following Baalim, and condemned him for killing Naboth and taking his vineyard.
Ahab sought Elijah in every nation and kingdom, and when Elijah came to him over Naboth's vineyard, Ahab said, Hast thou found me, O mine enemy?
Ahab took Jezebel to wife, and she stirred him up to work wickedness in the sight of the LORD.
When Naboth would not give up his vineyard, he was put to death and Ahab went down to take possession of it, and the LORD said to Ahab, Hast thou killed, and also taken possession?
Ahab said he hated Micaiah because he did not prophesy good concerning him but evil, and he had Micaiah put in prison and fed with the bread of affliction.
Scripture says Jehoshaphat joined affinity with Ahab, that is, became kin to him by marriage.
Jehoshaphat joined Ahab, saying, I am as thou art, and went with him to battle at Ramoth-gilead, and the seer asked him, Shouldest thou help the ungodly?
Ahaziah was Ahab's son, reigned in his stead, and walked in the way of his father.
Jehoram was the son of Ahab and reigned over Israel.
Hezekiah was Ahaz's son and reigned in his stead.
Ahaz was Jotham's son and reigned in his stead.
Pekah king of Israel came up to Jerusalem to war against Ahaz and besieged him, and slew a hundred and twenty thousand in Judah in one day.

Elijah told Ahaziah that because he sent to ask Baal-zebub, as if there were no God in Israel, he would not come down from his bed but would surely die, and he died according to the word of the LORD which Elijah had spoken.
Jehoshaphat joined himself with Ahaziah to make ships to go to Tarshish, and the LORD broke the works because he had joined himself with Ahaziah.

Ahijah tore his new garment into twelve pieces and told Jeroboam the LORD would give him ten tribes, and later told Jeroboam's wife the LORD would cut off his house; both came to pass according to the saying of the LORD by Ahijah.
Gedaliah was the son of Ahikam.
Amaziah was the son of Joash king of Judah and reigned in his stead.
Amaziah challenged Joash king of Israel, and Joash went up, smote Judah, took Amaziah at Beth-shemesh, broke down the wall of Jerusalem and took the treasures.
The people made Uzziah king in the room of his father Amaziah.
Jehoshaphat was Asa's son, reigned in his stead, and walked in all the ways of Asa his father.
Athaliah set out to destroy all the seed royal, and Joash was stolen away and hidden from her six years; when he was made king, she cried Treason and was slain.
Jehoiada's wife hid Joash from Athaliah so that she slew him not; in the seventh year Jehoiada made him king and commanded the captains to take Athaliah out and slay her.
Bathsheba bore Solomon to David, and when he was king Solomon rose to meet her, bowed to her, and set a seat for the king's mother on his right hand.
Nathan told Bathsheba, Let me give thee counsel, that thou mayest save thine own life, and the life of thy son Solomon, and sent her in to King David.
Benaiah brought Solomon down to Gihon to be anointed, carried out the king's commands, and Solomon put him over the host in Joab's place.
David sent Zadok, Nathan and Benaiah together to bring Solomon to Gihon and make him king, and they did it.
David sent Zadok, Nathan and Benaiah together to bring Solomon to Gihon and make him king, and they did it.
At Solomon's command Benaiah went to the altar, fell upon Joab and killed him.
At Solomon's command Benaiah went out and fell upon Shimei, and he died.
Solomon was born to David and Bathsheba; David made him king after him and charged him as his son to keep the LORD's charge.
Ornan offered David his threshing floor, oxen and wheat freely for the LORD's altar, but David paid him the full price and built the altar there.
David smote Hadarezer king of Zobah and took his chariots, horsemen and shields of gold, and later defeated the Syrians Hadarezer had sent out.
Rabshakeh came with a great host against Jerusalem, and Eliakim went out to answer him at the wall, where Rabshakeh mocked their trust in the LORD and threatened the men on the wall.
Eliakim son of Hilkiah was over Hezekiah's household, and Hezekiah sent him to Rabshakeh and to Isaiah.

Isaiah spoke the LORD's word that He would call His servant Eliakim the son of Hilkiah and commit the government into his hand, and later, when Eliakim was sent to him, Isaiah gave him the LORD's answer for Hezekiah.
After Elijah slew the prophets of Baal, Jezebel sent to swear she would take his life, and he fled for his life.
Elijah said the dogs shall eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel, and when she died Jehu said, This is the word of the LORD, which he spake by his servant Elijah.
Elisha went after Elijah and ministered unto him, and would not leave him until Elijah was taken up into heaven.
The LORD told Elijah to anoint Elisha to be prophet in his room, and Elijah cast his mantle upon him; the spirit of Elijah rested on Elisha.
Elijah's writing told Jehoram that because he had not walked in the ways of Jehoshaphat, had made Judah go a whoring, and had slain his brethren, the LORD would smite him and his people.
Gehazi was the servant of Elisha the man of God, who spoke for him to the Shunammite and went before him with his staff.
When Gehazi took Naaman's silver and lied about it, Elisha said, Went not mine heart with thee? and the leprosy of Naaman cleaved unto Gehazi.
Elisha sent word to Naaman to wash in Jordan seven times, and his flesh came again like the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.
When Hazael came to Elisha for Ben-hadad, Elisha wept for the evil Hazael would do to Israel and told him the LORD had shown him that Hazael would be king over Syria.
Elisha sent one of the children of the prophets with a box of oil to anoint Jehu king over Israel, and he did.
When Joash king of Israel came to the dying Elisha, Elisha had him shoot the arrow of the LORD's deliverance and told him he would smite Syria but three times.
Jehoshaphat asked for a prophet of the LORD, and for Jehoshaphat's sake Elisha spoke the LORD's word that the valley would be filled with water and Moab delivered into their hand.
Elisha told the king of Israel he would not look at him but for Jehoshaphat, then spoke the LORD's word to the kings that the valley would be filled with water and Moab delivered into their hand.
Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made Gedaliah ruler over the people he left in the land of Judah.
Gehazi ran after Naaman and lied that Elisha had sent him for silver and garments, and Naaman gave him two talents.
Joram went to war against Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth-gilead and was wounded when he fought with Hazael.
Hazael set his face to go up to Jerusalem, and Joash king of Judah sent him all the hallowed things and gold, and Hazael went away.
Hezekiah sent to Isaiah in the Assyrian crisis, and Isaiah brought him the LORD's word then, when he was sick unto death, and when he showed his treasures to Babylon's messengers.
Rabshakeh came with a great host against Hezekiah at Jerusalem, mocked his trust in the LORD, and told the people not to let Hezekiah deceive them.
Manasseh was Hezekiah's son and reigned in his stead, and built again the high places Hezekiah had destroyed.

Hilkiah the high priest carried out King Josiah's commands: he found the book of the law, went to inquire of the LORD for the king, and brought the vessels of Baal out of the temple at the king's command.
Hiram and Solomon made a league together; Solomon's builders and Hiram's builders hewed the stones and timber for the house, and Hiram's shipmen went with Solomon's servants to Ophir.
Hoshea the son of Elah made a conspiracy against Pekah, smote him, slew him, and reigned in his stead.
Jehoiachin was Jehoiakim's son and reigned in his stead.
Nebuchadnezzar came against Jerusalem and besieged it, and Jehoiachin went out to him, and Nebuchadnezzar took him and carried him away to Babylon.
The king of Babylon made Mattaniah, Jehoiachin's father's brother, king in his stead, and changed his name to Zedekiah.
Jehoiada's wife hid Joash six years in the house of God; then Jehoiada set a guard about him, and Jehoiada and his sons made him king and anointed him.
Joash did that which was right in the sight of the LORD all his days wherein Jehoiada the priest instructed him.
Pharaoh-nechoh made Eliakim the son of Josiah king in the room of Josiah his father, and turned his name to Jehoiakim.
Jehoiakim became Nebuchadnezzar's servant three years.
Jehoiakim turned and rebelled against Nebuchadnezzar, who came up against him and bound him in fetters to carry him to Babylon.
Jehoram was Jehoshaphat's son, and Jehoshaphat gave the kingdom to him because he was the firstborn.
Jehoram walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as did the house of Ahab, for the daughter of Ahab was his wife.
Jehoshaphat asked for a prophet of the LORD, Micaiah was sent for to the two kings as they sat at the gate of Samaria and prophesied there, and Jehoshaphat went to battle despite his word.
Joram asked Jehoshaphat, Wilt thou go with me against Moab to battle? and Jehoshaphat said, I will go up: I am as thou art.
Jehu conspired against Joram and drew a bow with his full strength and smote Joram between his arms, and had him cast into the field of Naboth.
Jehu called to Jezebel's eunuchs, Throw her down, and they threw her down, and he trod her under foot.
Jehu was among the men who rode after Ahab, and the LORD told Jehu to smite the house of Ahab his master.
Jeroboam was Solomon's servant, and Solomon made him ruler over all the charge of the house of Joseph.
Jeroboam lifted up his hand against the king, and Solomon sought to kill him, and he fled into Egypt until Solomon died.
When Rehoboam refused to lighten the yoke, Israel rebelled and made Jeroboam king, and there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all their days.
Jeroboam his son reigned in Joash's stead.
Jeroboam restored the coast of Israel from the entering of Hamath unto the sea of the plain, according to the word of the LORD, which he spake by the hand of his servant Jonah.
Jezebel wrote letters in Ahab's name to have false witnesses accuse Naboth, and he was stoned so Ahab could take his vineyard.
Jehu answered Joram, What peace, so long as the whoredoms of thy mother Jezebel and her witchcrafts are so many?
Solomon sentenced Joab to death for the innocent blood of Abner and Amasa, and had him killed at the altar.
Jotham his son was over the king's house, judging the people, while Uzziah was a leper, and reigned in his stead.
Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anointed Solomon king in Gihon at David's command.
David commanded Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet to anoint Solomon king, and Zadok and Nathan anointed him in Gihon.
The queen of Sheba came to prove Solomon with hard questions and told him all that was in her heart, and Solomon answered all her questions.
Rehoboam was Solomon's son and reigned in his stead.
Solomon bound Shimei by oath to stay in Jerusalem on pain of death, and when Shimei went to Gath, Solomon sentenced him and had him killed.
Zadok the priest took an horn of oil out of the tabernacle and anointed Solomon.
Solomon put Zadok the priest in the room of Abiathar.
Elijah foretold that the LORD would cut off Ahab's house and that dogs would eat Jezebel, and when Jehu did it scripture says the LORD had done that which he spake by his servant Elijah.
Ahaziah's mother's name was Athaliah.
Ahaziah walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother was his counsellor to do wickedly.
Ahaziah Jehoram's son reigned in his stead.
Jehu followed after Ahaziah and said, Smite him also in the chariot, and he died; the destruction of Ahaziah was of God by coming to Joram.
Ahaziah went with Joram to the war against Hazael and went down to see him in Jezreel when he was sick of his wounds.
Jehosheba took Joash the son of Ahaziah and hid him.
Amon was Manasseh's son, reigned in his stead, and walked in all the way his father walked in.
Josiah was Amon's son, and the people made him king in his stead.
The people took Jehoahaz the son of Josiah and anointed him king in his father's stead.
The king of Egypt made Eliakim his brother king over Judah, and took Jehoahaz away to Egypt.
Esther was taken to King Ahasuerus, who loved her above all the women and made her his queen.
Vashti was Ahasuerus's queen; when she refused to come at his command, a decree was made that she come no more before him.
King Ahasuerus set Haman above all his princes, and later had him hanged on the gallows Haman built for Mordecai.
Mordecai, who sat in the king's gate, uncovered a plot against King Ahasuerus, and the king later gave him his ring and made him next to himself.
The LORD sent Isaiah to tell King Ahaz to take heed, be quiet and not fear, and when Ahaz would not ask a sign, Isaiah gave him the sign of Immanuel.
The hand of Ahikam was with Jeremiah, so that he was not given into the hand of the people to be put to death.
Amos spoke the LORD's word against the house of Jeroboam, that Jeroboam would die by the sword, and Amaziah the priest reported his words to the king.
Baruch wrote the LORD's words from Jeremiah's mouth and did all that Jeremiah the prophet commanded him.
After King Jehoiakim burned the scroll Baruch had written, he commanded men to take Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah, but the LORD hid them.
Daniel told Belshazzar he had lifted himself up against the Lord of heaven and not humbled his heart, and read him the writing that his kingdom was finished.
Daniel 5 calls Nebuchadnezzar Belshazzar's father and says to Belshazzar, 'thou his son.'
Daniel called Hananiah (Shadrach) one of his companions; they were taken captive together, and Daniel asked him to pray with him for mercy over the king's dream.
Daniel called Mishael (Meshach) one of his companions; they were taken captive together, and Daniel asked him to pray with him for mercy over the king's dream.
Nebuchadnezzar made Daniel ruler over the whole province of Babylon and chief of the governors over all its wise men.
Daniel interpreted Nebuchadnezzar's dreams and told him, 'let my counsel be acceptable unto thee, and break off thy sins by righteousness.'
Darius set Daniel first of the three presidents over his kingdom and thought to set him over the whole realm; Daniel prospered in his reign.
Esther was the daughter of Mordecai's uncle, and Mordecai took her as his own daughter when her parents died.
Esther did the commandment of Mordecai as when she was brought up with him, and at his charge she went to the king for her people.
Esther named Haman before the king as 'the adversary and enemy' who had sold her and her people to be destroyed, and he was hanged.
The LORD told Ezekiel to set his face against Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, and prophesy against him.
The LORD told Ezekiel to set his face against Pharaoh king of Egypt and prophesy against him, and Ezekiel spoke the LORD's word that He would break Pharaoh's arms.
Nehemiah the governor and Ezra the priest and scribe together told the people the day was holy, and their days are named together.
Jeremiah was taken out of prison and committed to Gedaliah to carry him home, and Jeremiah went and dwelt with him at Mizpah.
Johanan warned Gedaliah that Ishmael was sent to slay him and offered to kill Ishmael to save him, but Gedaliah did not believe him.
The LORD told Hosea to take a wife of whoredoms, and he took Gomer, who bore him a son.
The word of the LORD came by Haggai to Zerubbabel, who obeyed it and built the house, and Haggai told him 'be strong, O Zerubbabel... and work.'
The word of the LORD came by Haggai to Joshua the high priest, who obeyed it, and Haggai told him 'be strong, O Joshua.'
Haggai and Zechariah prophesied together to the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem, and the elders built and prospered through their prophesying.
When Mordecai would not bow, Haman sought to destroy him and all the Jews and built gallows for him, but Haman himself was hanged on them.
Jehoiakim burned the scroll of Jeremiah's words and commanded men to take Jeremiah, but the LORD hid him.
Zedekiah asked Jeremiah in secret for the LORD's word, and Jeremiah gave him counsel: go out to the king of Babylon's princes and your soul shall live.

Jeremiah said the LORD would bring Nebuchadnezzar against the land and the nations would serve the king of Babylon seventy years, and Chronicles says the captivity in Babylon fulfilled the word by Jeremiah.
Johanan and the people asked Jeremiah to seek the LORD's way for them, and Jeremiah told them not to go into Egypt, but Johanan called his word false and took him to Egypt.
Jeshua and Zerubbabel together built the altar and began building the house of God in Jerusalem.
Zechariah saw the angel of the LORD take away Joshua’s iniquity and charge him to walk in the LORD’s ways, and at the LORD’s word Zechariah set crowns on Joshua’s head and told him of the BRANCH.

Meshach and Shadrach were both Daniel's companions; they were set over the province of Babylon together, refused together to worship the golden image, and were cast into the furnace together and delivered.
Nebuchadnezzar set Meshach over the affairs of the province of Babylon and, after the furnace, promoted him.
When Meshach would not serve his gods, Nebuchadnezzar in fury had him bound and cast into the burning fiery furnace.
Nebuchadnezzar set Shadrach over the affairs of the province of Babylon and, after the furnace, promoted him.
When Shadrach would not serve his gods, Nebuchadnezzar in fury had him bound and cast into the burning fiery furnace.
Nebuchadnezzar made Zedekiah king and made him swear by God, but Zedekiah rebelled against him.
Nebuchadnezzar besieged Jerusalem, and Zedekiah was brought to him at Riblah, where his sons were slain before his eyes and his eyes put out.
Sanballat mocked the rebuilding, conspired to fight against Jerusalem, and sought to draw Nehemiah out to do him mischief; Nehemiah counts him among 'our enemies.'
Tobiah was grieved at Nehemiah's coming, conspired against the work, and with Sanballat hired a prophet to make Nehemiah afraid; Nehemiah counts him among 'our enemies.'
Sanballat and Tobiah together scorned the rebuilding, conspired together against Jerusalem, and together hired a prophet against Nehemiah.
Zechariah brought the word of the LORD to Zerubbabel, 'Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit,' and said his hands would finish the house.
Eliphaz was one of Job's three friends who came to mourn with him and comfort him, and in the end Job prayed for his friends.
Bildad was one of Job's three friends who came to mourn with him and comfort him, and in the end Job prayed for his friends.
Zophar was one of Job's three friends who came to mourn with him and comfort him, and in the end Job prayed for his friends.
Elihu's wrath was kindled against Job because he justified himself rather than God, and he told Job, 'in this thou art not just.'
Bildad and Eliphaz were two of Job's three friends; they came together by appointment to comfort Job, and the LORD called Bildad and Zophar Eliphaz's "two friends."
Eliphaz and Zophar were two of Job's three friends; they came together by appointment to comfort Job, and the LORD called Bildad and Zophar Eliphaz's "two friends."
Bildad and Zophar were two of Job's three friends; they came together by appointment to comfort Job, and the LORD called them Eliphaz's "two friends."
Elihu's wrath was kindled against Job's three friends because they had found no answer and yet had condemned Job.
Elihu's wrath was kindled against Job's three friends because they had found no answer and yet had condemned Job.
Elihu's wrath was kindled against Job's three friends because they had found no answer and yet had condemned Job.
Malachi foretold the messenger who would prepare the way and the coming of Elijah, and Jesus said John the Baptist is that messenger and that Elijah.
Isaiah foretold the voice crying in the wilderness, and scripture says John the Baptist is the one Isaiah spoke of.
Isaiah foretold the Spirit-anointed preacher and the suffering servant, and scripture says these words were fulfilled in Jesus.

Jeremiah spoke the LORD's word against Coniah (Jehoiachin): he would be given into Nebuchadrezzar's hand, cast out with his mother to die in another land, and written childless as to the throne of David.
Jeremiah spoke of Rachel weeping for her children, and Matthew says Herod's slaughter of the children of Bethlehem fulfilled it.
David wrote in the psalms 'let their habitation be desolate' and 'let another take his office,' and Peter said the Holy Ghost spoke these by David concerning Judas.
Scripture calls Jesus Christ 'the son of David' and says He was made of the seed of David according to the flesh.
David wrote that God would not suffer His Holy One to see corruption, and Peter said David, being a prophet, spoke of the resurrection of Christ.

Abednego and Shadrach were both Daniel's companions; they were set over the province of Babylon together, refused together to worship the golden image, and were cast into the furnace together and delivered.

Abednego and Meshach were both Daniel's companions; they were set over the province of Babylon together, refused together to worship the golden image, and were cast into the furnace together and delivered.
Daniel called Azariah (Abednego) one of his companions; they were taken captive together, and Daniel asked him to pray with him for mercy over the king's dream.
Nebuchadnezzar set Abednego over the affairs of the province of Babylon and, after the furnace, promoted him.
When Abednego would not serve his gods, Nebuchadnezzar in fury had him bound and cast into the burning fiery furnace.
Joel foretold God pouring out His Spirit on all flesh, and when Peter and the disciples were filled with the Holy Ghost, Peter said this was what Joel had spoken.
Paul answered for himself before King Agrippa, who heard him and said Paul might have been set at liberty if he had not appealed to Caesar.
Festus laid Paul's case before King Agrippa and brought Paul before him so that he would have something to write to Caesar, and Agrippa told Festus that Paul might have been set at liberty.
Peter confronted Ananias for lying to the Holy Ghost about the price of his land, and Ananias fell down dead.
Ananias laid his hands on the blinded Saul at the Lord's command, and Saul received his sight and was baptized.
Ananias was a disciple at Damascus; the Lord Jesus spoke to him in a vision and sent him to Saul, and he went.
Andrew was Simon Peter's brother, and he brought Peter to Jesus.
Jesus chose Andrew as one of his twelve apostles.
Andrew was one of Jesus' disciples and followed him.
Andrew was one of John the Baptist's two disciples who heard him call Jesus the Lamb of God.
Aquila and Priscilla took Apollos aside and expounded the way of God to him more perfectly.
Priscilla and Aquila took Apollos aside and expounded the way of God to him more perfectly.
Priscilla was Aquila's wife.
Paul lived and worked with Aquila as a fellow tentmaker, and called him and Priscilla his helpers in Christ Jesus who had laid down their necks for his life.
Barnabas brought Saul to Antioch, where they taught together for a year, and the Holy Ghost sent them out together to preach.
Mark was Barnabas's sister's son.
Barnabas took Mark with him in the work, and when Paul would not take Mark again, Barnabas took him and sailed to Cyprus.
Jesus gave blind Bartimaeus his sight, saying his faith had made him whole.
Caiaphas counselled that Jesus should die, hosted the plot to kill him, and condemned him for blasphemy at his trial.
Caiaphas sat with the council that set Peter in their midst, questioned him about the healing of the lame man, threatened him and let him go.
An angel told Cornelius to send for Peter, who would tell him words whereby he and his house would be saved, and Peter preached Christ to them and had them baptized.
Demetrius stirred up the craftsmen and the city of Ephesus against Paul because his preaching was turning people from their idols.
Peter prayed and raised Dorcas from the dead at Joppa.
Elijah appeared with Moses on the mount of transfiguration and talked with Jesus about his coming death at Jerusalem.
Elisabeth was Zacharias's wife, and God gave them John in their old age.
The angel called Elisabeth Mary's cousin.
Filled with the Holy Ghost, Elisabeth blessed Mary and the fruit of her womb when Mary visited her.
Elisabeth bore John and named him.
The governor Felix heard Paul's case against his accusers, then deferred it and kept Paul bound for two years.
Paul was brought up at the feet of Gamaliel and taught by him according to the law.
Herod sought to destroy the child Jesus and killed the children of Bethlehem to do it.
John reproved Herod for taking Herodias, his brother Philip's wife, and for all the evil he had done.
Herod imprisoned John, would have put him to death, and finally had him beheaded.
Herod sought to kill Jesus, and at his trial he mocked him and set him at nought; scripture names him among those gathered against Jesus.
Scripture says Pilate and Herod were at enmity between themselves before Jesus' trial.
The day Pilate sent Jesus to Herod and Herod sent him back, Pilate and Herod were made friends together.
Herod killed James the brother of John with the sword.
Herod imprisoned Peter meaning to bring him out to the people, and the Lord delivered Peter out of Herod's hand.
James and John were brothers, the sons of Zebedee.
Jesus chose James as one of his twelve apostles.
James was one of Jesus' disciples and followed him.
James and John were partners with Simon in fishing.
James was named among Jesus' brothers and is called the Lord's brother.
The people of Nazareth named Mary as Jesus' mother and James among his brothers.
James and Peter led the Jerusalem church together, both called pillars by Paul and both speaking at the council.
James gave Paul the right hand of fellowship, that Paul should go to the heathen and they to the circumcision, and later Paul reported his work among the Gentiles to James.
Jesus chose Peter as one of his twelve apostles.
Peter was one of Jesus' disciples and followed him.
Jesus chose John as one of his twelve apostles.
John was one of Jesus' disciples and followed him.
John foretold one coming after him who was mightier than he, and then pointed to Jesus as the one of whom he had spoken.
Jesus chose Philip as one of his twelve apostles.
Philip was one of Jesus' disciples and followed him.
Jesus chose Matthew as one of his twelve apostles.
Matthew was one of Jesus' disciples and followed him.
Jesus chose Thomas as one of his twelve apostles.
Thomas was one of Jesus’ twelve disciples and followed him, saying he would go with him to die.
Pilate tried Jesus; he found no evil in him, yet he scourged him and delivered him to be crucified.
Mary was Jesus' mother; she brought him forth and stood by his cross.
Joseph took Mary as his wife and named her son Jesus, and with Mary raised him as his father.
Scripture says Jesus loved Martha; she received him into her house.
Scripture says Jesus loved Mary; she sat at his feet to hear his word and anointed his feet with costly ointment.
Scripture says Jesus loved Lazarus.
Jesus raised Lazarus from the dead after four days in the grave.
Jesus cast seven devils out of Mary Magdalene.
Mary Magdalene followed Jesus from Galilee and ministered to him, and was the first he appeared to when risen.
Moses foretold a prophet like himself whom the people must hear, and Peter preached that Jesus is that prophet; Jesus said Moses wrote of him.
Nicodemus spoke up for Jesus in the council, and after the crucifixion he brought spices and helped bury his body.
Jesus stayed at Zacchaeus's house and said, This day is salvation come to this house.
Simeon took the child Jesus in his arms, blessed God for him as His salvation, and said this child is set for the fall and rising again of many in Israel.
Saul breathed out threatenings and slaughter against the disciples, and Jesus told him, "I am Jesus whom thou persecutest."
Jesus appeared to Paul to make him a minister and witness, and Paul calls himself a servant of Jesus Christ.
Stephen was chosen from among the disciples, and as he was stoned he saw Jesus at the right hand of God and prayed, Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.
Zacharias was John's father; the angel promised him the son and he named him John.
John and Peter were fishing partners, and later went up to the temple together, healed the lame man, and were sent together to Samaria.
Joseph took Mary as his wife as the angel commanded.
Simeon blessed Joseph and Mary when they brought the child Jesus to the temple.
Jesus chose Judas Iscariot as one of his twelve apostles.
Judas was one of Jesus' disciples and followed him.
Judas betrayed Jesus to the chief priests for thirty pieces of silver and gave him up with a kiss.
Martha and Mary were Lazarus's sisters.
Mary, who anointed the Lord, was Lazarus's sister.
Lydia, baptized after hearing Paul, took Paul and his company into her house, and they returned there after their release from prison.
Mark went out with Paul and Barnabas, and later Paul called him a fellow labourer and profitable to him for the ministry.
Martha and Mary were sisters.
Simeon blessed Mary and Joseph in the temple and told Mary a sword would pierce her own soul.
Paul chose Silas and they went out together, were beaten and imprisoned together at Philippi, and sang praises in prison.
Timothy fully knew Paul's doctrine and manner of life, and Paul calls him his own son in the faith.
Paul took Timothy with him, and Timothy served with Paul in the gospel as his workfellow.
Saul kept the clothes of those who stoned Stephen and consented to his death.
Festus sat on the judgment seat and heard Paul's case, and when Paul appealed to Caesar, Festus sent him to Caesar.
Philip the evangelist took Paul and his company into his house at Caesarea for many days.
Peter rebuked Simon for trying to buy the gift of God with money and told him to repent.
Stephen and Philip were both chosen among the seven and appointed to the same business.
Simon believed Philip's preaching, was baptized, and continued with Philip.
Silas and Timothy stayed on together at Berea and then came together to Paul at Corinth.
Jesus chose Bartholomew as one of his twelve apostles.
Bartholomew was one of Jesus' disciples and followed him.
Jesus chose James the son of Alphaeus as one of his twelve apostles.
James the son of Alphaeus was one of Jesus' disciples and followed him.
Jesus chose Thaddaeus as one of his twelve apostles.
Thaddaeus was one of Jesus' disciples and followed him.
Jesus chose Simon Zelotes as one of his twelve apostles.
Simon Zelotes was one of Jesus' disciples and followed him.
Joseph of Arimathaea was Jesus' disciple, and he buried Jesus' body in his own new tomb.
Joseph and Nicodemus took Jesus' body together, wound it in linen with Nicodemus's spices, and laid it in the tomb.
As Jesus was led to be crucified, the soldiers compelled Simon of Cyrene to carry his cross after him.
Pilate offered the crowd Jesus or Barabbas; they chose Barabbas, who was released while Jesus was delivered to be crucified.
Barabbas was a prisoner who had committed murder in the insurrection, and Pilate released him to the crowd in place of Jesus.
Herod married Herodias, his brother Philip's wife.
Herodias had a quarrel against John and would have killed him, and she had her daughter ask for his head.
Sapphira was Ananias's wife, and she was privy to his lie.
Peter confronted Sapphira for agreeing with her husband to tempt the Spirit of the Lord, and she fell down dead.
Annas was father-in-law to Caiaphas.
After his arrest Jesus was led to Annas first, was questioned by the high priest about his disciples and his doctrine, and Annas sent him bound to Caiaphas.
Annas sat with the council that set Peter in their midst, questioned him about the healing of the lame man, threatened him and let him go.
Paul says he planted and Apollos watered, both ministers by whom the Corinthians believed.
Paul calls Luke one of his fellowlabourers, and near the end of his life Luke alone was with him.
Paul, who begot Onesimus in the faith in prison, pleaded with Philemon to receive him as Paul himself and charged any debt of his to Paul's account.
Paul calls Titus his partner and fellowhelper and his own son after the common faith.
Paul lived and worked with Priscilla and her husband, and called them his helpers in Christ Jesus who laid down their necks for his life.
Paul withstood Peter to his face at Antioch, because Peter withdrew from eating with the Gentiles and was to be blamed.
Paul calls Philemon his dearly beloved fellowlabourer.
Onesimus was Philemon's servant, whom Paul sent back to be received as a brother beloved.
Esau went to Ishmael and took Ishmael's daughter Mahalath to be his wife.
Adonijah was David's son by Haggith, born in Hebron, and his father had not displeased him at any time.
Mephibosheth was the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, and David restored him all the land of Saul.
Zedekiah the son of Josiah reigned instead of Coniah.
Jeremiah said the LORD would bring the people back after seventy years in Babylon, and the LORD stirred up Cyrus to send them home so that Jeremiah's word was fulfilled.
Micah foretold a ruler coming out of Bethlehem, and the scribes quoted his words as written of where Christ should be born.
Hosea wrote 'called my son out of Egypt,' and Matthew says Jesus being taken to Egypt and called out fulfilled what the LORD spoke by the prophet.
Zechariah foretold Zion's King coming lowly and riding on an ass, and Matthew says Jesus riding into Jerusalem fulfilled what was spoken by the prophet.
Gamaliel persuaded the council not to kill Peter and the apostles but to let them alone.
Matthew opens by naming Jesus Christ the son of Abraham.
